hints: Set \(t=\tan\theta\) and rewrite every trigonometric term using tangent identities.
Substitute these forms, clear denominators and simplify to a quadratic in \(t\).
Solve the quadratic, retain only values compatible with \(0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ\), and use \(\theta=\tan^{-1}t\).
walkthrough:
Let $t = \tan\theta$. Apply the compound angle formula for $\tan(\theta + 45^\circ)$:
$$\tan(\theta + 45^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan\theta + \tan 45^\circ}{1 - \tan\theta\tan 45^\circ}$$

Express $\cot 2\theta$ in terms of $t$ using the double-angle formula $\tan 2\theta = \dfrac{2t}{1 - t^2}$:
$$\cot 2\theta = \dfrac{1}{\tan 2\theta} = \dfrac{1 - t^2}{2t}$$

Substitute these expressions into the original equation:
$$t\left(\dfrac{t + 1}{1 - t}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{1 - t^2}{2t}\right)$$
$$\dfrac{t(t + 1)}{1 - t} = \dfrac{1 - t^2}{t}$$

Cross-multiply to clear denominators:
$$t^2(t + 1) = (1 - t)(1 - t^2)$$

Expand both sides of the equation:
$$\text{LHS} = t^3 + t^2$$
$$\text{RHS} = 1 - t^2 - t + t^3 = t^3 - t^2 - t + 1$$

Subtract $t^3$ from both sides and collect all terms on the left:
$$t^2 = -t^2 - t + 1$$
$$2t^2 + t - 1 = 0$$

Find the roots for $t = \tan\theta$:
$$2t - 1 = 0 \implies t = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$t + 1 = 0 \implies t = -1$$

Consider the required interval $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$:
In the first quadrant, $\tan\theta > 0$, so reject $\tan\theta = -1$.
Therefore, retain:
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
